current.text: He is likely Minnesota's sixth man and a scorer off the bench.
He is expected to play about 29 to 30 minutes off the bench. He may play more minutes than Josh Green and close games.
He might close games in small lineups instead of Jonathan Kuminga.
He shares the ball with LaMelo Ball and Anthony Edwards. Experts see him as the third offensive option at best, and they expect his usage to drop, which caps his upside.
Last season his 3P% rose from 33 to 44 and his FT% rose from 78 to 88. He also turned 71% of his deflections into steals.
Experts do not trust his shooting spike and expect his shooting and steal rates to come down. If he falls back to 49% from the field and 79% from the line, he is roughly a 140 to 180 player.
He is overvalued at his market rank of about 106 to 108 (round 9) and a fade at that price. He is fine around pick 135 or as a late grab.
One September point guard ranking puts him in tier 8.
Minnesota's bench has little scoring and no ball handlers, so he is the main scorer in the second unit.
Minnesota has a two-game week in the semifinal week of our playoffs (schedule 4, 2, 4 for a March 28 end).
Minnesota has 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.
Minnesota is expected to compete (one expert predicts 53 wins), so it should not rest players to tank.

durable.text: Steals and blocks are weak spots in his game.
His projected category line has no weak flag. FG% is his best category compared with other guards.

note: Both Yahoo and ESPN rank him 108 with average costs near 1 USD (values 4 and 2 USD), so in our auction he should be a 1 to 3 USD end-of-draft buy and not a target at a ninth-round price. He has no weak category and fits any build, but his value rests on last season's 51.7 FG% and 87.6 FT%; experts see him as a 140 to 180 player if that shooting falls back. Early in the season, check whether he gets 29 to 30 bench minutes and closes games, and whether his three-point and free-throw shooting holds.
